parameters.focus: SMS-only authentication users and users aged over 65 among the 3,950 patients still locked out
parameters.alternative_channels: call centre identity verification (95-minute queue, not listed as portal authentication fallback)

decision.rationale: 3,950 patients remain locked out, with the highest impact among SMS-only authentication users and users over 65. The call centre can verify identity but is not listed as a portal authentication fallback and has a 95-minute queue, so affected users lack a timely alternative channel. I will assess the access impact focusing on these groups and the call centre channel, and request network incident status from the telecom regulator to understand whether the outage is telecom-related and affecting SMS delivery. I do not know the root cause of the lockout, whether SMS delivery is impaired, or whether the call centre can be authorised as a fallback.

citations.relevance: Confidentiality obligations constrain any sharing of patient-related information, so access-impact recommendations must avoid disclosing patient account records.

The telecom regulator may be able to request information from the licensed operator about the network incident affecting public telecommunications service, which could help explain why SMS-only users remain locked out.

uncertainty: root cause of the patient lockout
whether SMS delivery to affected users is impaired
whether the call centre can be formally authorised as an authentication fallback
expected restoration time for portal access
